  "markdown_report": "At 0% progress, prioritize a small, testable extension: an ordered title encoder trained jointly with the corrected HSTU. No new validation improvement is claimed.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) User feedback distinguishes broad relatedness from specific usefulness. Titles may expose finer distinctions but cannot establish purchase intent or fulfilled needs. (2) Electronics’ 10.71% negative-over-positive rate and −0.0749 tenth-percentile margin motivate discrimination experiments, not conclusions about held-out ranking. (3) Collapse scores near 0.5 imply approximately zero mean cosine similarity. An anti-collapse intervention lacks supporting evidence.

**Insights from related work.** (1) HSTU supports gated representations and relative attention bias [1], allowing a small internal extension. (2) Kim’s word CNN [2] directly supports token-window features; character CNNs [3] instead share spelling fragments across identifiers. Neither guarantees compatibility. (3) MARS [4] supports attribute-aware matching but uses unavailable attributes and pretrained Longformer. It neither reproduces this proposal nor isolates pretraining effects. (4) Supplied text-permutation evidence [5] motivates alignment controls; WhitenRec [6] cautions that representation geometry can confound semantic attribution.

**Framework and directions.** Specificity can enter through item representation → ordered title residual; history selection → relative-position decay; optimization → normalized sampled softmax. Controls must distinguish additional capacity, item–text alignment and word order. Semantic alignment alone does not demonstrate order sensitivity.

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Positive and negative assessments follow.

| Atomic idea | Scores | Critical assessment across the five axes |
|---|---|---|
| Ordered title residual [2,4] | 4/7/8/7/6 | Originality: controlled integration; established components. Potential: reusable specificity; sparse supervision. User: targets broad matches and format distinctions; compatibility unproven. Model: targets Electronics confusion; transfer uncertain. Difficulty: compact module; controls and deployment require care. |
| Learned per-head position decay [1] | 3/6/6/5/3 | Originality: adaptive bias; familiar mechanism. Potential: recent intent; may suppress enduring interests. User: targets stale associations; fulfilled needs unobserved. Model: filters context; indirect evidence. Difficulty: few parameters; masking requires verification. |
| Normalized 128-negative softmax [1] | 2/6/4/8/4 | Originality: useful control; established recipe. Potential: discrimination; temperature sensitivity. User: potentially better ranks; no attribute signal. Model: targets separation; margins can mislead. Difficulty: conventional loss; additional scoring cost. |

**Selected experiment.** Retain the ordered title residual, baseline objective, sampler and optimizer. It explicitly targets broad thematic substitutions and overlooked format/connector distinctions, while testing Electronics’ measured confusion. Add width 1 for short titles and define padding-safe four-bin pooling. Keep one jointly trained HSTU/checkpoint per category.

Prioritize baseline versus title residual, then a matched order-invariant control. Budget permitting, separately retrain within-title permutations, frequency/length-stratified title reassignment and random item-code controls. Fixed shuffled titles can still identify items. Character features remain a later alternative for rare identifiers. Select solely by fixed macro validation HR@10; preserve seeds, budgets, diagnostics, routing and predictor parity. Report omitted controls and avoid attributing gains to semantics, order or compatibility without supporting evidence.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152 ; [2] https://aclanthology.org/D14-1181/ ; [3] https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.01626 ; [4] https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702 ; [5] https://github.com/dh-r/LLM-Sequential-Recommendation/blob/main/online_material.md ; [6] https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10602",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Add one small, jointly trained, order-sensitive title encoder to each corrected HSTU category model. Fuse its output into the item representation through a gate initialized near zero, using the same representation for history inputs and candidate scoring. Keep the baseline loss and sampling unchanged to isolate the representation intervention. Retain this as the first feasible experiment; treat character features, position decay and objective changes as separate later hypotheses.",
    "motivation": "The selected idea explicitly addresses two observed user failures: broad thematic matches replacing specific preferences, and recommendations overlooking format or connector distinctions. It also targets the measured Electronics negative-over-positive rate of 10.71%, tenth-percentile margin of -0.0749, and small-margin rate of 16.36%. These observations motivate a hypothesis; neither improved compatibility nor improved validation HR@10 has been demonstrated. The prior inspiration used unordered text pooling plus several objective and sampling changes; this proposal isolates ordered title features as a smaller first experiment. Revised originality/potential/difficulty scores are 4/7/6: the components have direct prior art, the controlled specificity question remains useful, and reproducible controls plus checkpoint/predictor consistency require more work than the small encoder alone suggests. User/model alignment scores of 8/7 reflect relevance to the supplied diagnoses, not measured efficacy.",
    "implementation_notes": "Extend the supplied corrected HSTU rather than replacing its backbone. Keep its architecture dimensions, optimizer, loss, sampling, validation schedule and checkpoint rule fixed for the first comparison. Train exactly one independent network per category, with all four required routes: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl. No independent text predictor, score fusion, checkpoint averaging or separately fitted popularity/transition component is permitted. Every control is a separate experiment and must satisfy the same single-model constraint.

Use only supplied public titles for this experiment; descriptions remain a separately documented extension. Do not use the generic examples' unavailable reviews, ratings, prices, stores or item categories. Build title assets only from the metadata scope made available by the host, without interaction labels from validation or test. Record that scope, missing-title coverage and truncation rates. Text availability alone does not establish compatibility or explain a user's choice.

Use Unicode NFKC normalization followed by lowercase conversion and tokenize with the exact Python pattern r"[^\W_]+(?:[./-][^\W_]+)*|[^\w\s]", using Unicode matching. This retains token order and internal decimal points, hyphens and slashes, including strings such as 3.5mm and usb-c; isolated punctuation is also retained. Reserve PAD=0 and UNK=1. Count document frequency once per item title, retain tokens appearing in at least two titles, cap the vocabulary at 50,000 including reserved entries, and order retained tokens by descending document frequency with lexical tie-breaking. Keep the first 32 tokens and right-pad title tensors. These title tensors are distinct from the required left-padded interaction histories. Save normalization, pattern, vocabulary, token tensors, original/truncated lengths and missing-title masks. Vocabulary truncation can collapse rare identifiers to UNK; this is a known weakness rather than evidence that the encoder models exact identifiers.

Use 32-dimensional randomly initialized token embeddings with a zero padding row, and stride-1, no-padding Conv1d branches of widths 1, 2 and 3, each with 32 output channels, a learned bias and ReLU. Width 1 preserves one-token titles. For a title containing n retained tokens, a width-h window starting at s is valid only when s+h <= n and every token in the window is nonpadding. Mark all other windows invalid, mask their activations to negative infinity before max pooling, and return a zero vector when a bin has no valid windows. Zero input padding alone is insufficient because convolution biases can yield positive padded activations.

Assign each valid window to bin min(3, floor(4*(s+(h-1)/2)/n)), where s is zero-based. Max-pool each channel within each of the four bins; concatenate in width-major then bin-major order, producing 384 features. Apply a bias-free linear projection to the baseline item dimension, followed by LayerNorm with eps=1e-5. Set e(i)=item_emb(i)+sigmoid(g)*residual(i), with one learned scalar g initialized to -3. Apply the missing-title mask after LayerNorm so empty titles always produce a zero residual despite learned affine parameters. Force e(0)=0 and preserve the baseline's padding-embedding handling. Use e(i) for both history encoding and candidate scoring, retaining all baseline score scaling and normalization. Text features are internal layers of the single model and receive gradients only through its recommendation loss. A nonzero title residual still changes initial scores; initialization near zero does not make the starting network exactly identical to the baseline.

The token CNN is directly related to Kim (2014), although its widths and positional pooling differ from that paper's global pooling. The character-CNN paper provides an alternative architectural precedent, not a direct description of this token encoder. Coarse positional pooling retains some location information but does not reliably represent arbitrary connector direction, number-unit bindings or physical compatibility. A shallow character encoder could share rare alphanumeric fragments, but introducing it now would add another intervention. Defer it unless measured title coverage and identifier errors justify a separate budgeted experiment.

Keep item_emb as the ID embedding module for the ModelView compatibility contract. Expose joint vectors through the actual model and make predict_score use them. Preserve log2feats(sequence), the family-specific sample_batch, and the diagnosis loader tuple (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) must retain their interfaces. Return both metrics and metric_definitions, and construct the interpretation prompt from measured values and their definitions. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Operational margins must use predict_score; distinguish raw-ID embedding similarity from joint-vector similarity. Leave unsupported metadata breakdowns unavailable. A mapped cosine score near 0.5 is not evidence of substantial directional collapse. Preserve the baseline definitions and sampling when comparing diagnostics; any new metrics need explicit definitions. Changed score scales can make raw margin comparisons misleading.

Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per executed epoch. Retain the host environment default SASREC_EPOCHS=200 despite its generic variable name, and enforce the maximum. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save artifacts beneath the trial directory. Retain supplied splits and the pinned evaluator: 200 validation users per category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42. Select using macro validation HR@10, not Electronics diagnostics. Train on a single GPU. All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials count against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not access test labels, hidden test files, other trials' artifacts or external datasets/pretrained weights.

Before execution, record the corrected baseline's actual optimizer settings, architecture, initialization, sampler, validation cadence and checkpoint rule in the experiment manifest. This proposal inherits them from the host rather than inventing missing values. Reset training RNGs to 42 per category and use dedicated seed-42 generators for control transformations, so preprocessing changes do not inadvertently advance the training RNG. Preserve baseline parameter initialization where possible by initializing the additional branch with a separate generator. Record deterministic settings, versions, parameter counts, measured runtime and all attempted configurations. A matched number of updates does not imply matched wall-clock cost.

Prespecify the experiment order: corrected baseline comparison; title residual; then, if affordable, an order-invariant control. For that control, use one width-1 convolution with 384 output channels, global masked max pooling and the same 384-to-d projection, LayerNorm and gate. Its convolution has exactly the same parameter count as the three width-1/2/3 branches: 32*(32*(1+2+3)+3)=6,240 parameters. It matches branch dimensions and trainability while removing token order, but changes feature allocation, so it is not a perfect isolation of order. Hold optimization settings and update budgets fixed; report parameter and compute differences elsewhere rather than calling controls universally matched.

If budget permits, separately retrain three additional controls. First, permute nonpadding tokens independently within each title using a dedicated generator seeded 42, traversing items by ascending internal ID; save the fixed permutations. This preserves token multisets and lengths but changes local patterns, and fixed shuffled titles can still identify items. Second, reassign complete tokenized titles across items within training-frequency deciles and title-length quartiles. Form deciles by sorting on (training interaction count, item ID), divide into equal-count rank bins, then form length quartiles within each decile by sorting on (truncated token count, item ID). Keep missing-title items separate, permute within each resulting stratum with a dedicated seed-42 generator, and record unchanged singleton strata. This preserves title collections and approximately controls popularity/length while breaking item–text alignment; it does not exclude every identity shortcut. Third, replace title tokens by fixed random nonpadding vocabulary IDs drawn uniformly with seed 42, preserving each item's token count, missingness, vocabulary dimensions and the entire trainable branch. This tests whether an extra item-identifying code can explain gains; its token-frequency statistics differ from real text, so interpret it alongside the reassignment control. Each control requires retraining; inference-only scrambling introduces distribution shift.

A separately trained parameter-matched ID-only control is also useful, but no unique architecture is implied by that phrase. If attempted, specify and report the ID-only capacity increase explicitly; prioritize the random-code control, which directly preserves the branch structure. Do not silently alter HSTU width to claim exact matching. Stop adding controls when their expected cost cannot fit the remaining shared budget, and report omitted controls. The baseline/title contrast establishes only the effect of the full extension, not semantics or order separately.

Measure validation head/tail differences using training-interaction-count strata and report stratum sizes, history lengths and missing-text coverage. TASTE motivates popularity analysis but does not establish that this proposal reduces popularity bias. Track title-branch contribution norms and their associations with popularity and title length to detect shortcuts; define these as descriptive diagnostics. If per-user validation hits are available, report paired within-category bootstrap intervals using 10,000 replicates with a dedicated seed-42 analysis RNG, averaging the four category means in each replicate. Such intervals condition on one training seed and fixed candidates and do not remove repeated-selection optimism. One changed validation-user hit changes macro HR@10 by 0.125 percentage points. Do not select on these diagnostic strata or substitute them for the host metric.

For left-padded histories, read the maximum position index with a nonzero item, never nonpadding_count-1. Handle empty histories using the corrected baseline convention. Save one selected checkpoint per category containing model parameters, complete architecture configuration and title assets. Update the embedded predictor writer with the identical encoder, fusion, normalization, score scaling and four-category routing. In evaluation mode, verify training-model and reloaded-predictor scores agree on permitted examples, including short/missing titles, left-padded histories and the baseline empty-history case. Record the maximum absolute difference and numerical precision. Any cached text vectors must be computed from that same selected checkpoint after training and invalidated when parameters change; they are an implementation cache, not an independently fitted predictor.

Report all attempted trials and actual validation results. The supplied earlier combined_score=0.5887 is not evidence for this revised encoder and should not be relabeled as its measured performance. Preserve the native simulator's five training users per category and full-catalog unseen-item recommendations when that stage is run. Sampled validation HR@10 and training margins do not establish full-catalog usefulness, semantic reasoning, fewer compatibility rejections or awareness of fulfilled needs. Establish those claims only with appropriate measured user evidence.",
    "pseudocode": "Prespecify baseline settings, experiment order, checkpoint rule and remaining GPU budget.
For each affordable, separately trained experiment:
    For each of the four supplied category routes:
        Retain preprocessing seed 0 and the supplied splits.
        Build deterministic title assets from host-permitted metadata only.
        Apply any prespecified control using a separate seed-42 generator.
        Reset training RNGs to 42 and initialize the corrected HSTU.
        Initialize the additional branch with a separate generator.
        Define title_encoder(tokens):
            Apply trainable 32-dimensional token embeddings.
            For width h in [1, 2, 3]:
                Compute 32-channel convolution followed by ReLU.
                Mark only fully nonpadding windows valid.
                Assign each valid window to its specified center-position bin.
                Mask invalid windows before max pooling.
                Return zeros for bins without valid windows.
            Concatenate width-major/bin-major outputs into 384 features.
        Define joint_item(i):
            residual = LayerNorm(bias_free_projection(title_encoder(tokens[i])))
            Zero residual after LayerNorm for missing titles and padding.
            vector = item_emb(i) + sigmoid(g) * residual
            Force padding vector to zero.
            Return vector.
        Use joint_item for sequence inputs and candidate scoring.
        For each configured epoch, capped at 200:
            For exactly 200 batches:
                Sample causal examples with the supplied HSTU sampler.
                Compute HSTU features and the unchanged baseline objective.
                Update the single network jointly with the baseline optimizer.
            Validate only at the unchanged schedule using the pinned protocol.
            Apply the prespecified baseline checkpoint rule.
            Account for training, diagnosis and failed-run GPU seconds.
        Save one selected checkpoint, configuration and title assets.
        Run compatible diagnosis using actual predict_score margins.
        Return measured metrics and their definitions.
    Write working/predict.py using the identical architecture and routing.
    For inference:
        Load exactly one checkpoint for the requested category.
        Compute log2feats(left_padded_sequence).
        Gather the maximum nonpadding position; handle empty input explicitly.
        Score candidates through the model's single predict_score function.
    Verify reloaded score parity on permitted examples and record differences.
Report actual macro validation HR@10, attempted/omitted controls and GPU costs.
Attribute gains to alignment or order only when the corresponding controls support it.
Never combine separately trained experiments at inference.",
    "originality": {
      "score": 4,
      "positive": "The controlled integration tests whether ordered, position-sensitive title features improve specificity within one HSTU while separating capacity, alignment and order explanations.",
      "negative": "Word-window CNNs, positional pooling, gated residual fusion and attribute-aware recommendation are established. The contribution is an experimental adaptation rather than a new architectural principle."
    },
    "future_potential": {
      "score": 7,
      "positive": "Provides a feasible route to test observable item specificity without pretrained weights or independent predictors, with informative controls that could guide later character-level or recent-intent extensions.",
      "negative": "Sparse titles, rare identifiers, brand shortcuts and weak interaction supervision may limit transfer. Sampled HR@10 improvements would not establish physical compatibility, fulfilled-need awareness or full-catalog usefulness."
    },
    "code_difficulty": {
      "score": 6,
      "positive": "The encoder is compact and leaves the corrected HSTU blocks, baseline objective and sampler intact; all features belong to one jointly trained model.",
      "negative": "Padding-safe positional pooling, deterministic controls, efficient repeated item encoding, diagnostic adaptation, budget accounting and exact checkpoint/predictor consistency require substantial implementation and verification."
    }
  },
